questions.question: In synchronous digital circuits, which fundamental component is used to store a single bit of information?
Which of the following statements accurately describes a key difference between Static RAM (SRAM) and Dynamic RAM (DRAM)?
options: SRAM is typically used for main memory (RAM) due to its high density, while DRAM is used for CPU caches due to its speed.
SRAM requires periodic refreshing to maintain data, whereas DRAM retains data as long as power is supplied.
DRAM cells are typically larger and more complex, using 6 transistors per bit, while SRAM cells are simpler, using a capacitor and a transistor.
SRAM is faster and more expensive per bit than DRAM, making it suitable for CPU caches.
DRAM is volatile memory, losing its data when power is removed, but SRAM is non-volatile.

questions.question: In the digital IC design flow, what is the primary purpose of **Static Timing Analysis (STA)**?
options: To generate the physical layout (GDSII) of the circuit after routing.
To verify the functional correctness of the design by simulating its behavior with test vectors.
To mathematically prove or disprove temporal logic properties of the design, ensuring correctness without simulation.
To check for and ensure that all timing constraints (e.g., setup time, hold time, clock frequency) are met across all operating conditions without running dynamic simulations.
To identify and fix design rule violations (DRC) and layout versus schematic (LVS) mismatches.

questions.question: In an out-of-order execution processor, what is the primary architectural technique used to eliminate "write-after-write" (WAW) and "write-after-read" (WAR) data hazards, thereby allowing more instructions to execute speculatively and in parallel?

In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, as feature sizes shrink to deep sub-micron and nanometer scales, the precise fabrication of desired circuit patterns becomes increasingly challenging due to wave-like properties of light during lithography. Which phenomenon specifically describes the degradation of printed feature fidelity (e.g., line width variations, corner rounding) compared to the ideal mask pattern, even with ideal focus and exposure?
